notes: Company background: multichannel contact center platform used by ~120 enterprise customers; sells both SaaS and managed services.
Primary driver: deliver consistent agent-assist latency during peak spikes (Black Friday-type surges) and guarantee isolation for enterprise clients.
Workload profile: 24/7 support operations, global coverage. Typical steady-state: ~800 concurrent agent sessions; peak surges tested up to 4,200 concurrent sessions for large customers.
Targets: sub-150ms token turnaround for token-level assist paths, 200-300ms P95 for short assistant responses. Ticket summarization acceptable up to 2s per ticket in batch jobs.
Throughput: estimate 1.2M tokens/day baseline, burst capacity required up to 6M tokens/day for promotions/spikes. Need reserved throughput to avoid throttling.

Model preferences: prefer open models with improved instruction-following; willing to run quantized Llama2-variants or similar. Wants Redwood model catalog recommendations for cost/latency trade-offs.
Routing/fallback: must fallback to smaller low-cost model when dedicated pool saturated; automatic regional failover to EU/NA replicas required for geo-residency customers.
Security & compliance: strict residency for EU customers, KMS support for key management, detailed audit logs for every call, SSO/SAML for internal users.
Integration needs: tool-calling hooks to CRM (Zendesk/ServiceNow), ability to call internal tools via secure function-calls; robust rate-limits per tenant.
POC scope (requested): 1 week of steady-state + 3 days of controlled surge testing; include canary rollout and rollback behavior; include tracing and per-token cost dashboard.
Cost sensitivity: medium-high — willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit economics are clear; wants Optimize recommendations (batching, KV cache) baked into PoC.
Quote from CTIO on 2026-02-14: 'We need predictable latency under load, not just average numbers. If you can show P95 guarantees we'll move forward.'
Operational concerns: on-call rotation for incident response, runbook alignment with Redwood's SLAs, charting of tail-latency during rollouts.
